title: Don’t Judge Code by Its Cover: Exploring Biases in LLM Judges for Code Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Inserting single-line comments into the source code that falsely imply the code was written by an expert developer.
Adding explicit assertions of correctness, such as the comment '# correct code', at the beginning of the code snippet.
Applying an automated code transformation that systematically replaces semantically meaningful variable names and function parameters with randomized alphabetic strings.
Inserting single-line comments implying that the author of the code lacks expertise (e.g., stating it was written by a beginner).
Using an LLM to generate and insert single-line comments that inaccurately describe the functionality of the original code, anchoring the judge to a false internal description.
Artificially inflating the perceived complexity and length of the code by declaring dummy functions at the beginning that are never actually called or used within the logic.
